description:
Why is quitting smoking so hard, and what actually helps? Cyto breaks it down from the 6ix for Addictions Awareness Week and Lung Cancer Awareness Month.

In the Italian RISP lung cancer screening program, 7,805 current smokers were offered a quit program. Among 1,375 who chose the plant-based medicine cytisine, 50.1% quit, versus 8.1% of 2,173 who had counselling alone (adjusted OR 14.5). Common side effects were nausea (36%), insomnia (19%) and abdominal discomfort (18%).

The catch: this was NOT a randomized trial. People chose cytisine themselves and were more motivated, so the gap overstates the drug. A 2026 review says cytisine works better than placebo in randomized trials, is broadly similar to varenicline, and was added to the WHO Essential Medicines list in 2025. Availability differs by country, so ask your doctor or pharmacist what is available to you.

Sources (via PubMed):
Cani et al., J Thorac Oncol 2026 - https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jtho.2026.104071
Diana et al., Pulm Ther 2026 - https://doi.org/10.1007/s41030-026-00402-w

Not medical advice. Free quit support in Canada: search Smokers' Helpline (Canadian Cancer Society) or ask your pharmacist.
